To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

leaf growth parameters of Coffea arabica trees are affected by the seasonal variation in air temperature, water availability and CO2 concentration and that these effects differ among the tree structure and between the leaf types (sun and shade).
(1) the leaf area of the tree structure is a key parameter for the growth of the tree structure.

(i) the seasonal variation in leaf expansion rates is not related to changes in leaf water potential, but to seasonal variations in air temperature and CO2 concentration, and to the availability of water, (ii) the leaf expansion rates of adult trees are not uniform throughout the canopy, but vary with the leaf age, and (iii) these variations are related to the leaf position on the branch and to the branch position on the tree.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the growth of leaves and the factors affecting it.
the effects of water availability, air carbon dioxide concentration, and their interaction, on the growth of adult coffee trees.
understanding the effects of environmental factors on the growth of the leaves and branches of the coffee tree.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide on the physiology, growth and development of trees are highly complex, and are influenced by a number of factors including the species, age, size, and environmental conditions under which the tree is growing.
the growth of coffee is affected by the amount of light available to the tree.
the effects of CO2 on the physiology of plants are complex, but the overall trend is a stimulation of plant growth and yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tree structure of coffee trees is highly variable, and that leaf size and leaf area index vary in relation to seasonal and environmental variables.
the growth of coffee trees is highly plastic, responding to a wide range of biotic and abiotic factors.
leaf growth is not only affected by the environment but also by the position of the leaf in the tree.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of trees is not uniform across the canopy.
the effects of CO2 enrichment on tree growth and leaf physiology depend on the tree’s position in the canopy.
we can use a combination of leaf growth measurements and leaf gas exchange data to estimate the effects of climate change on the carbon balance of a tree.
